summary: Mrs. Hidary explores the development of the holiday of Sukkot by tracing its mentions in the Torah as both an agricultural festival and a historical commemoration. She explains how the combination of these two aspects on the 15th of Tishrei creates a unique opportunity for unity and happiness. The class also discusses the significance of the Torah readings chosen for the Shabbat of Sukkot.
questions: Why does the Torah describe Sukkot as both an agricultural festival and a historical one?
How can the Torah command someone to be happy?
Why do we read about Moshe and the 13 attributes of God on the Shabbat of Sukkot?
What is the significance of combining the farmer's holiday with the shepherd's holiday?
